seo_title: Delhi HC Rejects Bias Challenge to POSH Committee
title: Delhi High Court: Mere Apprehension of Bias Not Enough to Disqualify a PoSH Internal Committee
case_name: Dr. XXXXXXXX and Anr. v. University of Delhi and Ors.
card_summary: Two associate professors of Kalindi College, University of Delhi, challenged a fresh Internal Committee set up to inquire into a sexual harassment complaint against them, alleging bias in its constitution. Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma dismissed the petition, holding apprehension of bias must rest on cogent evidence of a real likelihood, not suspicion alone, and let the fresh inquiry proceed.
card_tip: An employee or institution objecting to an Internal Committee's composition under the PoSH Act needs concrete evidence of actual bias in a specific member, not a general apprehension, to get the committee reconstituted.
verification_notes: The petitioners (two Kalindi College associate professors), the judge (Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma), the decision date (27 October 2026) and the core holding on apprehension of bias are reported consistently by Devdiscourse and Careers360. The case number, W.P.(C) 13218/2026, is drawn from the Delhi High Court's own judgment file name (SKS27102026CW132182026), which independently corroborates the judge's initials and decision date. Sources differ on whether the fresh inquiry was given 60 or 90 days to conclude, so this card states only that a time limit was set without stating the figure.
